chunks: Muhammad ibn Qays narrated from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام gave judgment concerning a female slave whom the son of her master had sold while her father was absent. The one who bought her took her as a concubine, and she bore him a boy. Then her first master came disputing with her later master and said, "My slave-girl was sold by my son without my permission." He said, "The ruling is that he may take his slave-girl and her son." Then the one who had bought her appealed to him and said to him, "Take his son who sold to you," and you say, "No, by Allah, I will not release your son until you release my son." So when the master of the slave-girl saw that, he approved the sale of his son.

key_terms.أَجَازَ: he ratified or approved, thereby validating the transaction
key_terms.الْحُكْمُ: the legal ruling or judgment issued in the case
key_terms.بَيْعَ: sale; the transaction under legal consideration
key_terms.بِغَيْرِ إِذْنِي: without my permission; indicating lack of legal authorization
key_terms.وَلِيدَةٍ: a female slave-girl at the center of the ownership dispute
key_terms.يُخَاصِمُ: he disputes or litigates against another party

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling when a slave is sold without the owner's permission and later the owner approves the sale?
ai.summary: This hadith records a legal ruling from Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام regarding the sale of a female slave by someone lacking authorization from the owner. It shows the judicial handling of disputed ownership, the consequences for the child born from that union, and the eventual ratification of the sale by the original owner.
